name: Petros Moutsos
bio: Petros Moutsos was a young Greek seaman and member of the Federation of Greek Maritime Unions (outlawed in Greece) who walked off his ship in 1955 and married an American. Held for deportation under the McCarran-Walter Act on a charge resting largely on his refusal to discuss his political affiliations, he was secretly put aboard a plane to Greece in April 1957 but was rescued in Paris; the immigration board itself conceded his union membership 'might be punishable by death.'
charges: Deportation under the McCarran-Walter Act — to Greece

name: Steve Tandaric
bio: Steve Tandaric was a pioneer CIO steel organizer and a veteran of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade who fought Franco in Spain, pursued for deportation for two decades. Arrested by federal agents in March 1957 and held without bail at the Chicago Detention Center, he won a stay pending judicial review of the 1951 deportation order against him.
charges: Deportation under the immigration / McCarran Internal Security Act — for radical labor and anti-fascist activity
convicted: Final deportation order (1951); arrested and held for deportation 1957
sentence: Deportation detention; denied bail; stay won pending review

name: Peggy Wellman
bio: Peggy Wellman was the wife of the convicted Michigan Smith Act defendant Saul Wellman, whom the government sought to deport to Canada — where she had been born during her mother's brief visit, though she had lived in the United States all her life. Her case went before the Circuit Court of Appeals in 1957.
charges: Deportation under the McCarran-Walter Act — to Canada

name: Rebecca Maisenberg
bio: Rebecca Maisenberg was a Detroit woman the government moved to denaturalize under the Walter-McCarran Act for alleged political associations. Her case, paired with that of former Michigan state senator Stanley Nowak, went to the U.S. Supreme Court as a test of the Act's denaturalization provisions (Maisenberg v. United States, 1958).
convicted: Denaturalization ordered; on appeal to the Supreme Court

name: Andrew Yiannopolis
bio: Andrew Yiannopolis was a Greek-born Chicagoan, director of the Greek Theater and a 42-year U.S. resident, ordered deported under the Walter-McCarran Act for alleged past Communist Party membership. In 1957 the Seventh Circuit upheld a district court ruling quashing the deportation, finding he had been denied a fair hearing and that the salaried government witnesses lacked credibility.
charges: Deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act — for alleged Communist Party membership
convicted: Ordered deported; deportation quashed on appeal (1957)

name: Hazel Wolf
bio: Hazel Wolf was a Canadian-born Seattle woman — later a celebrated environmental organizer — subjected to repeated deportation proceedings for alleged past Communist Party membership. In 1957 she won a stay of the government's sixth deportation attempt in eight years, her attorney arguing she had been wrongly classified as an alien.
charges: Deportation under the immigration laws — for alleged past Communist Party membership

name: Walter Baer
bio: Walter Baer was a Seattle engineer and Depression-era activist for the unemployed, ordered deported to Germany under the McCarran-Walter Act on the pretext of two trivial 1919 bad-check charges — proceedings the American Committee for Protection of Foreign Born tied to his old battles with private power interests. After 23 years' jeopardy, deportation was halted in 1957 when the governor of Oregon granted him an unconditional pardon.
charges: Deportation under the McCarran-Walter Act — on 'moral turpitude' pretext
convicted: Final deportation order; halted 1957 by gubernatorial pardon

name: Rodolfo Lozoya
bio: Rodolfo Lozoya was a Mexican-American shop steward and disabled Air Force veteran, in the U.S. 29 years, refused re-entry from Juarez in January 1957 as an 'excludable alien' charged with Communist Party membership under the McCarran-Walter Act. Stranded in Mexico and threatened with arrest and prosecution if he crossed, he left a wife and seven U.S.-born children on relief in Chicago.
charges: McCarran-Walter Act — exclusion for alleged Communist Party membership
convicted: Barred re-entry January 1957; awaiting a hearing
sentence: Excluded from the U.S.; threatened with arrest

name: Stella Brown
bio: Stella (Stefana) Brown was a Detroit grandmother, brought from Poland at age two and naturalized in 1946, sentenced to six months for contempt for refusing on Fifth Amendment grounds to inform on relatives and friends while testifying in her own denaturalization trial. The U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear her appeal.
charges: Contempt of court — for refusing to inform during her denaturalization trial
convicted: Sentenced to six months for contempt; on appeal to the Supreme Court
